From: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@pulseai.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — follow-up on TTFT & streaming

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful. A couple of items we wanted to follow up on from the product side so we can qualify the SLOs:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): ideal target would be <= 50ms on average, with 95th percentile under 120ms for our interactive flows.
- Throughput/concurrency: currently planning for ~100 sustained concurrent users (each opening a streaming connection), but we expect spikes up to ~300 during peak events.
- Streaming: we plan to use WebSocket for low-latency UI updates. Chunk cadence expectation is roughly every 100-200ms (small partial chunks for progressive UI).

Can Redwood support those numbers on a hosted plan, or would we need Dedicated? If possible, could you share a short SLO template and any perf test results for TTFT/streaming cadence?

Also, curious about fallback behavior — if TTFT degrades, do you have model variants or routing policies we could use to maintain the user experience?

Thanks,
Sam

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 3:04 PM Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@pulseai.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful. A couple of items we wanted to follow up on from the product side so we can qualify the SLOs: ...

Recap / answers at a high level:
- TTFT: We can get TTFT in the sub-100ms range for many open models on Redwood Hosted when using streaming optimized kernels and our prefix/KV cache. Hitting <=50ms 95p will depend on model choice and underlying GPU class; for strict guarantees we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity + GPU profile guarantee).
- Throughput/Concurrency: 100 sustained concurrent streaming connections is achievable on Hosted with burst capacity in most regions; spikes to ~300 are a good candidate for Dedicated (or Hosted + autoscaling/burst + routing to model variants).
- Streaming & chunk cadence: WebSocket is fully supported (SSE also supported). Chunk cadence is a function of model decode step size and batching; we can tune decode chunk size and batching window to target 100-200ms cadence for many models.

Attachments I'm including: redwood-slo-template.pdf (SLO + monitoring fields), ttft-test-instructions.md (how we run a TTFT + streaming cadence test).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick technical sync (30 min) with Aditya from infra to capture expected prompt sizes, avg response tokens, and peak concurrency — propose Wed 10:00-10:30am PT.
2) We'll run a controlled TTFT + streaming harness using your sample prompts (we'll share results and 95/99p numbers).
3) If results look good, we'll draft a scoped Dedicated config or a Hosted sizing recommendation + rollout plan.

Can you confirm Fri the 30th 10am PT for the technical sync, and attach a sample prompt set (or point us to the Drive link)?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sam — looping in a few technical questions so we size the perf test correctly. A couple of asks from our infra/perf side: 

1) Payload sizes: can you share typical prompt token counts and average generated token counts (rough estimate is fine). This impacts batching and KV cache behavior.
2) Client behavior on partial chunks: do clients render partial tokens as they arrive, or only render at sentence/completion boundaries? If partial rendering is required, we may tune decode step size smaller.
3) Preferred protocol: you mentioned WebSocket — any constraints on keepalive or maximum connection idle time?
4) Traffic pattern: are spikes evenly distributed across users (many simultaneous new sessions) or concentrated to a smaller subset of heavy users?

Plan: once we have numbers we'll run a test harness that measures: TTFT (1st byte), 95/99p TTFT, chunk cadence median/95p, and decode-latency per-chunk. We'll share test-run artifacts and a recommended config (model variant, batch window, quantization profile).

I've attached ttft-test-instructions.md with the exact benchmark steps and the harness repo link. If you can drop a sample prompt set to the Drive link Marissa mentioned, we'll schedule the run for tomorrow morning.

Thanks,

From: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@pulseai.com>

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLO follow-up — technical Qs

Thanks — answers below.

- Prompt size: ~60 tokens on average (range 20-150).
- Generated response: ~120 tokens average.
- Client rendering: we render partial chunks as they arrive (progressive UI). So smaller, frequent chunks are preferred.
- Protocol: WebSocket preferred, clients tolerate a 30s idle timeout but prefer keepalive pings.
- Traffic pattern: mostly even across users, but during product announcements spikes come from many concurrent new sessions. Expect sustained 100 concurrent streaming sockets and spikes to ~300 for 60-90s windows.

- Target SLOs: practical target is TTFT <=80ms (95p <=150ms); ideal is <=50ms if achievable.

I've uploaded a small sample prompt set and a recent smoke test log to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/ttft-tests-7543. Also attached pulseai-smoke-logs.zip with client-side timestamps.

If you run the harness tomorrow morning and can share the results by EOD, we can align on Dedicated sizing if required.

Appreciate the quick response — looking forward to the test results.

Sam
